fact: The National Department of Health states that the District Health Management Information Systems (DHMIS) Policy for South Africa was adopted in July 2011 to make implementation uniform across the country, with standard operating procedures and a National Indicator Data Set governing data flow from facility to national level.

The National Digital Health Strategy 2019-2024, signed by the Minister of Health on 15 May 2019, names the DHIS as the routine system for tracking public-sector health service delivery, established in 1996/97, and as a component of the comprehensive HMIS the sector is working towards.

The strategy states that cutting primary healthcare registers from more than fifty to six standardised registers lightened the data capturing workload at facility level, and that South Africa has moved from DHIS 1.4 to WebDHIS; it dates neither, so the date is the strategy's signing.

The National Digital Health Strategy 2019-2024 makes a complete electronic health record its first digital health priority and commits to a roadmap for a national EHR that integrates existing solutions on a common platform, to be achieved by 2024.

The strategy is published by the National Department of Health, which it makes responsible for facilitating and coordinating implementation, including the electronic health record, by provinces, districts and municipalities.

The National Department of Health states that the diagnostic, treatment and billing modules needed for a patient electronic health record are yet to be developed, the patient registration system being only its first prerequisite.
